notes: Direct RunBattleEffect10 sibling in the battle-effect dispatcher.
Fresh cross-edition analysis measures 230 executable bytes plus final owner alignment and proves the 186-byte normalized core is identical in all six GS1 editions.
Ranked ahead of the other unresolved sub-432-byte RunBattleEffect siblings by exact-length proximity and current wrong-instruction count.
The complete initial candidate is two bytes short and remains broad in allocation and loop-carrier formation; it is preserved as evidence but is not adoptable.
Adoption requires zero differing halfwords in all six editions.

Follow-up investigation (no candidate change, documenting a new concrete lead): re-diffed the existing candidate.c with candidate-show and traced the very first divergence to the `Data_02000240 + 500` address computation for the object-id lookup. The reference computes this at runtime (`movs r2,#250; ldr r3,[pc]; lsls r2,r2,#1; adds r3,r3,r2; ldr r0,[r3,#0]` -- i.e. 250<<1=500 synthesized in registers then added), but this project's toolchain folds `extern u8 Data_02000240[]; ... Data_02000240 + 500` into a single pre-computed absolute-address pool constant at compile time (confirmed by compiling the byte-exact template games/gs1/src/graphics/palette/adjust_bank.c against its own exact owner 0x080aac84, which shows the toolchain WILL fold a similar 'symbol + compile-time-constant offset' expression when the offset is small enough to matter, and separately confirmed on main:080941e0 in this same batch where `((s16*)Data_02000240)[247]` also got folded instead of computing 247*2 at runtime). This means the real ROM source almost certainly does NOT write this access as `Data_02000240 + 500` / an array-typed index -- some other spelling (a genuine runtime-computed byte offset the compiler cannot prove constant, e.g. built from a non-constant-propagated intermediate, or Data_02000240 accessed through a pointer variable rather than a direct symbol) avoids the fold in the reference. This is the single largest concrete lead for closing this owner's gap and should be tried before further register-level tuning on the existing candidate.c.

Follow-up (candidate rewritten, progress but not adopted): the non-constant-propagated-intermediate lead above was confirmed directly. games/gs1/src/object/motion/set_action_callback.c line 34-35 (`index = 250; ... Object_GetById(*(u32 *)&Data_02000240[index]);`, Data_02000240 declared `extern s16 Data_02000240[]`) is the exact idiom: assigning the literal into a local `s32 index` variable first, then indexing through it, defeats this compiler's constant folding and reproduces the reference's `movs r2,#250; lsls r2,#1; adds r3,r3,r2` runtime address build exactly. Also fixed: Func_0808ba1c (= object/table/get.c's ObjectTable_Get) takes a u32 id by value, not a void*, so the call is `object = Func_0808ba1c(*(u32 *)&Data_02000240[index]);` (a plain 4-byte load of the id, not a `void **` dereference). The same `index = 147;` idiom (through an `s32 *` cast of Data_02000240) reproduces the second runtime `movs r2,#147; lsls r2,#2` computation for the `Data_02000240+588` store later in the function. Fixing both closed the first ~30% of the diff (107 -> 91 differing halfwords) and made the object/record/entry prologue byte-identical through the first `bl Func_08009080`. Also established (by testing): `record + 38` should be written as an in-place pointer mutation (`record += 38;` then used as `*record`), not a second named `second_flag` pointer variable -- the mutated-pointer form scores strictly better (91 vs 95 differing halfwords) and matches the reference's reuse of the same hard register for the pre- and post-mutation value. Remaining residual (91/232 differing halfwords, candidate still exactly 2 bytes/1 halfword short) is now concentrated entirely in one register-allocation choice in the loop preamble and body: the reference spills `first_flag` (record+37) to an extra stack slot (`sub sp,#8` instead of `#4`) and additionally threads `record` (post `+=38`) through `fp` as a long-lived home with a separate low-register copy (`r5`/`r6`) materialized once before the `do`/`while` and reused for all 10 iterations, whereas this compiler keeps both pointers directly in low registers (r6/r7) for their entire lifetime with no spill and no fp involvement. Tried and empirically ruled out (all produced byte-identical output to the 91-diff candidate, confirming the scheduler/allocator -- not statement order -- picks this shape): every valid reordering of `first_flag=record+37 / record+=38 / object[108]=0 / cycle=0` that keeps the first two in sequence; reusing `cycle` (reset to 0 after the loop) as the source value for both `entry[5]=0` and the final `*(s16*)(state+382)=0` (reference does visibly reuse one register, r8, for both, but rewriting the C to alias them through `cycle` produced identical asm, so the reuse is CSE-driven, not source-shape-driven); declaring `first_flag` before vs after `entry`. No PERM_GENERAL-testable source variant found that reproduces the extra stack slot; this looks like it hinges on GCC 2.96's own live-range-weight heuristic for a value referenced both inside and after a loop, which has not been pinned down from the C side. Next session should look at whether a genuinely different C shape for the two flag writes (e.g. threading them through a small helper the compiler can't inline, or a struct-typed record instead of an offset-indexed `u8 *`) changes the weight; not yet tried.

Follow-up (large jump, candidate now length-exact but still not zero-diff): the struct-typed-record idea flagged above as untried was tried and is the fix. Replacing the offset-indexed `u8 *record` + `record += 38` mutation with a 2-field struct (`typedef struct { u8 pad[37]; u8 flag_a; u8 flag_b; } Record; Record *record = *(Record **)(object + 80);`, writes via `record->flag_a` / `record->flag_b`) made the compiler reproduce the reference's exact `sub sp,#8` extra stack slot, the `fp`-homed long-lived pointer, and the r5/r6 loop-local copies -- differing_halfwords dropped from 91 to 54 in one step, with the object/record/entry prologue through the entire do/while loop now byte-identical (matched_prefix extends through the loop and its exit compare/branch). Separately, reusing `cycle` (reset to 0 after the loop) as the actual source value for both `entry[5] = cycle;` and the final `*(s16 *)(state + 382) = cycle;` -- which previously (before the struct fix) produced byte-identical output to the plain-literal-0 form and looked like pure CSE -- turned out to matter once the struct fix was in place: with the struct-typed record, aliasing both stores through `cycle` reproduces the reference's r8-cached-zero reuse across both sites and pushed the candidate to candidate_bytes == owner_bytes == 232 (previously 228, 4 bytes short) with differing_halfwords down to 36 and matched_prefix = 66 (of ~116 total halfwords). This confirms the earlier 'CSE, not source-shape' conclusion about the cycle-reuse trick was an artifact of testing it against the wrong (non-struct) base shape, not a fact about the compiler. Current file (232 == 232 bytes, 36/232 differing halfwords) is the best reached this session; NOT adopted (not zero-diff). Remaining residual is a single, well-isolated cluster right after the loop, in the `Func_08099678` callback setup for `Func_080041d8(Func_08099678, 0xc80)`: the reference loads the callback's address into a scratch register early (`ldr r5,[pc,#80]`) and copies it into r0 only immediately before the `bl` (`adds r0,r5,#0`) -- two instructions, with the load visibly hoisted/scheduled ahead of the `movs r6,#1` / `*first_flag=1` sequence that follows it -- while this compiler instead loads the address directly into r0 in one instruction, right at the call site, and picks r5 instead of r6 for the '1' constant since r5 is left free. Everything else in the 36-halfword residual (a few pc-relative pool-offset renumberings, the branch-target shift, and a single `movs r0,r0` alignment pad near the very end) is mechanical fallout from that one instruction-count difference, not a separate defect. Tried and empirically ruled out (every variant below produced byte-identical output to the 36-diff candidate, i.e. this compiler's own optimizer already collapses them back down -- so this is a scheduler-pass behavior, not something reachable by reasonable source reshaping): introducing an explicit `void *cb = Func_08099678;` (both function-scope, which also badly perturbed the already-matched prefix via global register pressure, and block-scoped immediately around the call, which had no effect at all); mimicking the exact sibling idiom in games/gs1/src/map/colosso/log_rolling_stage/start_palette_task.c (`{ s32 budget = 0xc80; s32 task = ...; Func(task, budget); }`, both field orders) which only shuffled the single ldr's position without adding the second instruction; a `register`-qualified local for the callback; moving `index = 147` earlier; writing the pointer as `(void *)&Func_08099678`; and swapping the `flag_a`/`flag_b` post-loop write order (this one is NOT a scheduling-neutral no-op -- it regresses hard, back to 84 differing halfwords / 228 bytes, confirming `flag_b = 2;` must precede `flag_a = 1;` after the loop, matching the reference's `strb r7,[r2,#0]` before the first_flag reload). Next session's best lead: find what makes GCC 2.96 hoist a load ahead of independent scalar stores in a way that also frees a low register for reuse -- likely tied to some larger-scale property of the function (total instruction/pool count parity, or a genuinely different statement earlier in the same block) rather than the callback expression's own spelling, since every direct rephrasing of the callback expression alone was neutralized by the optimizer.
